author: bshastry
content: We found an unfixed corner-case, deposits: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/a0619b279aa57140768859767be392ff5a20f656/packages/types/src/gloas/sszTypes.ts#L242

author: tbenr
content: and don't we have a similar issue in beacon block body? in GLOAS, "deposits" must be 0 but it is enforced only at gossip\stf

author: bshastry
content: Yeah, the linked line from lodestar is exactly the deposits deserialization but checked late leading to memory amp from blocks under max payload size with a large number of deposits (~8k)

author: nflaig
content: we can probably limit that to 0 in the container, but generally, can't you do the same with deposit requests, since those are unbounded?

author: bshastry
content: Yes, I think so. The deserialization DoS primitive is not limited to beacon block gossip with non-canonical deposits

author: nflaig
content: but I don't think we can limit the deposits requests anymore, so the limit there is the max gossip limit

author: bshastry
content: The spec leaves out deposit requests check: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md#new-verify_execution_requests_limits

author: bshastry
content: Aha, understood. They are intentionally left out in CL specs because they are gas bound in the EL 🙏

author: bshastry
content: I can confirm that even with Teku's conservative 10 message byte-cap for unknown parent block roots, lots of beacon block gossip with about 50k deposit requests each can DoS a teku node with 32GB RAM and 8GB heap limits. Requires about 500 beacon block gossip messages. The byte-cap helps but the issue is in deserialization. Sig check does not help because it happens too late

author: tbenr
content: yeah.. i have an alternative version of that PR that applies the limits deeper in the ssz, close to each field. But with such approach reference tests need big changes. Let's talk about these stuff later in ACDT

author: nflaig
content:
<@504202741933932544> regarding the spec test harness, we added this handler
```ts
// Only an ssz list limit violation is an expected input error, anything else is a decode bug
shouldErrorOnInput: (error: Error, inputNames: Set<string>) =>!inputNames.has("post") && /over limit/.test(error.message)
```
so the `inputNames.has("post")` is what Justin mentioned, and we have a specific error message in our ssz lib

author: tbenr
content: so you have a map ( test -> expectedError ) for each of those tests?

author: nflaig
content: yeah it's not very nice, works for now though, we should probably encode this on the spec side the same way as clients do if everyone is going to enforce this during deserialization anyways
